title: Monolithic high density integrated photonics on bulk lithium niobate
authors: Zizheng Li, Harmen Smedes, Bruno Lopez-Rodriguez, Thomas Scholte, Simon Groeblacher, Iman Esmaeil Zadeh
abstract: Functional electro-optic (EO) tunable photonic integrated circuits are crucial to next-generation information processing and advanced computing, where ferroelectric materials such as lithium niobate (LiNbO3) provide outstanding optical properties and versatile tuning mechanisms. However, beyond achieving high-performance devices, practical deployment of LiNbO3 photonic integrated circuits requires rapid and cost-effective scale-up, which remains challenging because of the fabrication complexity and high costs of ion-sliced thin-film lithium niobate and wafer bonding processes. To address this gap, we demonstrate a fully monolithic photonic platform, amorphous silicon carbide (a-SiC) on bulk LiNbO3 crystal substrate, enabling scalable, CMOS-compatible, low-cost, and high-density photonic integrated circuits without relying on thin-film LiNbO3. This integration approach breaks the long-standing cost-performance-scalability tradeoff, and intrinsically eliminates the need for sophisticated fabrication processes, including ion slicing, wafer bonding, and LiNbO3 etching. It realizes high-density, low-loss, and record high EO tuning efficiency of VpiL = 2.87 Vcm on bulk LiNbO3 crystal substrate. Furthermore, leveraging slow-light effect near photonic crystal bandgap, an 8.5-fold EO tuning efficiency enhancement is achieved, highlighting the platform's capability in confinement control and dispersion engineering.
summary: This work introduces a breakthrough monolithic platform by integrating amorphous silicon carbide ($	ext{a-SiC}$) waveguides onto bulk lithium niobate ($	ext{LiNbO}_3$). This approach bypasses the high cost and complexity of traditional thin-film $	ext{LiNbO}_3$ processing, enabling scalable, low-loss photonic circuits. The platform achieves record electro-optic tuning efficiency and demonstrates advanced control over light dispersion using Photonic Crystal structures.
main_problem: The primary challenge is developing scalable, cost-effective, high-density photonic integrated circuits using lithium niobate while circumventing the fabrication difficulties and high costs associated with traditional thin-film $	ext{LiNbO}_3$ processing.
main_result: The authors demonstrate a fully monolithic platform ($	ext{a-SiC}$ on bulk $	ext{LiNbO}_3$) that achieves record high electro-optic tuning efficiency ($	ext{V}_\pi	ext{L} = 2.87 	ext{ V}\cdot	ext{cm}$) and shows an $8.5$-fold enhancement via slow-light effects.
method: The approach involves depositing amorphous silicon carbide ($	ext{a-SiC}$) onto a bulk $	ext{LiNbO}_3$ substrate using CMOS-compatible processes, allowing for the patterning of waveguides and photonic crystal structures in $	ext{a-SiC}$ while retaining high performance from the underlying bulk crystal.
model_or_system: The physical system is an integrated photonics chip built on a bulk lithium niobate ($	ext{LiNbO}_3$) substrate, utilizing amorphous silicon carbide ($	ext{a-SiC}$) for patterning and light guiding. The platform supports various devices including microring resonators, racetrack resonators, and Photonic Crystal (PhC) structures.
key_observables: Electro-optic tuning efficiency ($	ext{V}_\pi	ext{L}$), propagation loss ($1.3 	ext{ dB/cm}$), thermo-optic tuning slope ($39.54 	ext{ pm/K}$), and the achievable slow-light enhancement factor.
important_parameters: The process operates below $300^\circ	ext{C}$, ensuring CMOS compatibility; key parameters include waveguide dimensions, lattice constants for PhCs, and the electro-optic coefficients of $	ext{LiNbO}_3$.
main_assumptions: The fabrication process assumes that patterning in $	ext{a-SiC}$ does not significantly degrade the optical properties or structure of the underlying bulk $	ext{LiNbO}_3$ crystal.
figures_summary: Figures detail the multi-step, CMOS-compatible fabrication flow ($	ext{a-SiC}$ deposition, RIE patterning, metal liftoff) and show SEM cross-sections of the resulting waveguides. Other figures illustrate characterization results for resonance dips, thermal tuning, and electro-optic responses.
paper_structure: The paper details the novel monolithic $	ext{a-SiC}/	ext{LN}$ fabrication flow, presents measurements of passive components (resonators) showing low loss, characterizes active devices like PhC-based MZIs for high EO tunability, and discusses leveraging slow-light effects via PhCs.
why_interesting: While the core topic is photonics engineering rather than fundamental quantum theory, the precise control over light confinement, dispersion engineering (via PhCs), and electro-optic modulation efficiency ($	ext{V}_\pi	ext{L}$) are crucial enabling technologies for future quantum photonic circuits and quantum information processing.
